guidelines.title: 24.02 Classification of Captain Black - Little Cigars
guidelines.text: These are goods consisting of two parts: one part is for smoking, made of processed tobacco, cut and wrapped in a wrapper of homogenized tobacco leaf. The second part is a filter mostly made of acetate. The goods are marketed in a pack of 20 units, each unit with a length of 100 mm, a diameter of 8 mm, and a weight excluding the filter not exceeding 1.3 grams. The goods in question are cigarettes and are classified accordingly under subheading 24.02.2000. Effective from 21.8.2006 023/18.

guidelines.title: 24.02 Classification of Captain Black - Little Cigars
guidelines.text: These are goods consisting of two parts: one part is for smoking, made of processed tobacco, cut and wrapped in a wrapper of homogenized tobacco leaf. The second part is a filter mostly made of acetate. The goods are marketed in a pack of 20 units, each unit with a length of 100 mm, a diameter of 8 mm, and a weight excluding the filter not exceeding 1.3 grams. The goods in question are cigarettes and are classified accordingly under subheading 24.02.2000. Effective from 21.8.2006 023/18.

Inspection travel can be actuated via the PL640 toggle switch. Toggle switch position 1 (lever left) 2 (lever right) Function Normal operation Inspection travel With inspection travel turned on, no further travel commands are taken on. The car can only be moved by pressing the up and down keys. Inspection travel can only be activated when the safety circuit is closed. As such, it cannot be used for retrieval, for instance, from the emergency limit switch. The in-use lamps flash at the landing doors when inspection travel is ongoing. BKG ! Caution! Operating modes Moving the car as part of inspection travel means there is no automatic lift stopping at the end stops. The lift either travels up to the emergency limit switches or lands on the mechanical stoppers. On completion of the maintenance work, the PL640 printed circuit board toggle switch must be made use of to turn off the inspection travel. The printed circuit board cover is put back on and from a push-button panel a travel command is sent to either the top or bottom floor. 13 Functions 3 Functions 3.1 Visual display 3.1.1 Location indicator The location indicator tells the user where the lift currently is. BKG 4 Connection and Setting 4.1 Control panel 4.1.1 Assembly in the machine room 4 Warning - Risk from electrical current! Connection and Setting Some of the control system and electrical component voltages are potentially lethal. Touching live parts can lead to very serious injuries and may be lethal! Therefore: • • Mains switch and/or building-side fuses are to be isolated before the control panel is removed from the guiding section. Only when the control panel has been mounted in the guiding section is the voltage to be turned on again. To make it easier to get at the equipment in the machine room, the control panel can be moved on the guiding section or taken from it and mounted on the machine room door. Once the maintenance work is over, the control panel is to be put back into the guiding section. 4.1.2 Controller in the control cabinet The controller can also be fitted into a control cabinet which is optionally available. An additional mains switch must be installed in the machine room if the control panel cannot be seen from it. 4.2 Installation of the shaft wiring The floor junction boxes are to be fitted at the floors in keeping with the lift drawing. A floor junction box is part of each floor. The boxes are equipped at the floors in keeping with the actual appliances and are marked from X1 to X27. Box X1 is at the lowest floor and Box X27 at the uppermost. Boxes X2 – X5 - if present - are assigned to the middle floors. The floor junction box contains the PL625 safety circuit printed circuit board and the PL621 control printed circuit board. The floor junction boxes are connected by the control and safety cables. To this end, the cables are installed through the corner rod of the shaft structure and secured with clamps. The circuit and wiring drawings form the basis for the electrical installation of the floor junction boxes and equipment on the floors. The equipment cables at the floors are directed into the floor junction boxes and linked via connectors with the appropriate PL621 / PL625 printed circuit boards. The equipment connecting cables are installed at the shaft structure belts and secured with cable bands. To relieve tension, the cables are to be fixed with cable bands at the floor junction boxes. The cable bands are to be pulled through the ports at the side of the floor junction boxes and the cables fixed to them. 17 BKG Connection and Setting ! Caution - Damage to cables! The cables are to be installed well away from the car, counterweight, door locks and other moving components. During installation the bending radii are to be adhered to. Any pronounced kinks in the cables are to be avoided. Bending radius = 4 x cable diameter. 4.3 Floor switch 4.3.1 Lifts with 2 stops Pointer The lift drawing specifies where the floor junction box is located. All cable lengths have been calculated for this arrangement. Any other arrangement of the shaft installation might result in the calculated cable lengths being no longer adequate. The car position is recorded by the floor switches. A floor switch is assigned to each floor. Bi-stable solenoid-operated switches are used. The solenoid-operated switches are proximity-connected via 2 actuating magnets. Switching is done as a function of poling and direction. It is vital that the following points are followed when undertaking installation: • • • • The solenoid-operated magnet is to be fitted so that the connecting cable hangs down. Note the positions of the actuating magnets! Red magnet at the top, green magnet below. Actuating magnet and solenoid-operating switch are not to be over 10mm apart. With the lift stopped, the solenoid-operating switch is located between the red and green actuating magnets. The solenoid-operated switches are set at 50%b capacity. Select the actuating magnet spacing so that the solenoid-operated switch is between the red and green actuating magnet once the lift stops. The solenoid-operated switches are now to be moved on the holding devices so that the lift stops flush with the floors. 4.3.2 Lifts with 3 to 6 stops 18 The solenoid-operated switches are set at 50%b capacity. Adjustment work is begun at one of the middle floors. Select the actuating magnet spacing so that the lift stops between the red and green actuating magnets. The spacing of the actuating magnets is now reduced to the extent that the lift stops at the same position whether going down or going up. In going down, the lift stops when the green actuating magnet is reached. In going up, the lift stops when the red actuating magnet is reached. Only now are the solenoid-operated switches at the floors to be moved on the holding devices to the extent that the lift stops flush with them. BKG Connection and Setting Pointer To improve the arriving precision of <= 0.1 m/s lifts, two solenoid-operated switches are connected in parallel in the middle floors. The solenoid-operated switches are operated via 2 separate magnetic tracks. 4.4 Mounting the trailing cable ! The trailing cable contacts the car electrical equipment with the controller. There is a mounting bracket under the car for fastening the trailing cable. The trailing cable is directed into the car junction box and secured with cable bands. Halfway up the shaft, the trailing cable with its holder is fastened to a shaft structure belt and then run all the way to the controller. The trailing cable is electrically installed on the basis of the circuit and wiring plans. Caution - Damage to the trailing cable! The trailing cable must be twist-free and hang well away from the structure in the shaft. With the car in the end positions, the trailing cable is to hang freely. It must not be under tension or lie on the bottom of the shaft pit. The bending radius of the trailing cable is to be adhered to. All safety switches are connected in series. The safety circuit contacts are, on no account, to be parallel-connected or bridged. Warning! Risk of injury from bridging the safety circuit! Bridging the safety circuit or individual safety switches can lead to serious injuries and even to fatal ones. Therefore: Never bridge the safety circuit or individual safety switches! The locking circuit is arranged downstream of the safety circuit and controls door locking. (only applies to lifts with magnetic locking cams.) Various safety switches may be used depending on the lift type. The lift safety switches can be seen from the circuit diagrams. A PL625 safety circuit printed circuit board can be found in every floor junction box. Plugs connect the safety switches to the printed circuit board. Plug-in connections are to correspond to the specifications of the circuit and wiring plans. Flat connectors are used for connecting up the PE conductor. Assignment of the plug-in connections: 3-pin grey 2-pin grey Riser line Plug-in connection Safety switch 2-pin black Plug-in connection Locking switch Flat connector PE conductor connection 4.5.2 At the car 20 Terminal blocks are used to connect up the safety switches at the car in the car junction box. The car safety switches are brought together in the car junction box and connected to the controller via the suspended cable. Connection is by means of terminal blocks which are to correspond to the specifications of the circuit and wiring plans. BKG Connection and Setting 4.5.3 Checking the safety switches ! 4 Warning! Risk of injury from faulty safety and locking circuits! A faulty safety circuit can lead to serious injuries which may be fatal. Therefore: Check on every safety and locking switch as to working order. Warning - Risk from electrical current! Risk to life from electrical current! There is a direct risk to life from coming into contact with energized parts. Therefore: Only have work on the electrical system carried out by electrical skilled workers. • Do not bridge the safety switches. • • Electrical safety equipment tests must be carried out to comply with EN81- 3 Annex D. Examine each safety switch on the basis of the circuit diagram and a suitable measuring instrument. 4.6 Drive unit connection A Warning - Risk from electrical current! Some of the control system and electrical component voltage is potentially lethal. Touching live parts can lead to very serious injuries and may be lethal! Therefore: • • • Isolate mains switch and fuses on the building side prior to connecting the controller to the mains network. Check on isolation from power supply. Secure against the mains switch being turned on again. Before connecting the controller to the mains network it must be ensured that • • • All electrical components and modules are effectively connected to the protective circuit. All metallic components - in particular the shaft structure - are effectively connected to the equipotential bonding provided by others. All safety switches are connected and in working order. Caution - Damage to components! Check on the following before connection to the supply network: • • Does the mains voltage conform with the lift specifications? It is absolutely necessary that the specification requirements of the lift for the building-side fusing are adhered to! To relieve tension, the leads are to be fixed with cable bands at the control panel. rules.rule_text: This part does not include: Composite bars for railway or tramway (heading/subheading 86.08) or other items in Chapter XVII (Vehicles, Aircraft, Vessels and Associated Transport Equipment). [References: chapter XVII – Section XVII: VEHICLES, AIRCRAFT, VESSELS AND ASSOCIATED TRANSPORT EQUIPMENT]
Rules for Section XVI: This Section does not include: Items in Part XVII; [References: section XVII – Section XVII: VEHICLES, AIRCRAFT, VESSELS AND ASSOCIATED TRANSPORT EQUIPMENT]
For the purpose of classifying goods in this Chapter, the weight shall be considered as the weight of a motor vehicle in a condition fit for operation.

A motor vehicle will be classified in subheading 87.03.2150 and in subheading 87.03.9050 if it has four wheels which are connected directly, without suspension, to a front axle with steering and to a rear axle driven by an engine; the diameter of its wheel rim does not exceed 6 inches; its length does not exceed 205 cm; and the height from the floor (without the seat and without the headrest) does not exceed 65 cm.
Heading/subheading 86.07 refers, inter alia, to rail vehicles.

[References: chapter XVII – Section XVII: VEHICLES, AIRCRAFT, VESSELS AND ASSOCIATED TRANSPORT EQUIPMENT]
Rules for Section XVI: This Section does not include: Items in Part XVII; [References: section XVII – Section XVII: VEHICLES, AIRCRAFT, VESSELS AND ASSOCIATED TRANSPORT EQUIPMENT]
For the purpose of classifying goods in this Chapter, the weight shall be considered as the weight of a motor vehicle in a condition fit for operation.

A motor vehicle will be classified in subheading 87.03.2150 and in subheading 87.03.9050 if it has four wheels which are connected directly, without suspension, to a front axle with steering and to a rear axle driven by an engine; the diameter of its wheel rim does not exceed 6 inches; its length does not exceed 205 cm; and the height from the floor (without the seat and without the headrest) does not exceed 65 cm.
Heading/subheading 86.07 refers, inter alia, to rail vehicles.
